output:
**The Thursday Tea Trolley: Two Places on the Rota**

I have been helping with the tea trolley in the day therapy unit at Wensum Vale on a Thursday since March 2022, and we are two people short. If you have been wondering what volunteering here involves, I can tell you exactly what it involves, because I have been doing it and I am not a particularly impressive specimen of a volunteer. I am seventy-four, I retired from forty-one years of bookkeeping for a builders' merchant in Dereham, and before I started here I had no regular reason to go out of the house most weeks. I drifted about for eighteen months. Thursdays fixed that.

Here is the job. The day unit sees somewhere between fourteen and eighteen patients on a Thursday. Some come for the art group, some for hand massage, some for the company, and most of them go home afterwards. The trolley goes round from half past one and we finish at four.

The commitment is one Thursday a fortnight — every other week, on the rota. The rota was built for six of us. We are currently four. One left in the summer to be near her grandchildren in Sheffield, and one is having a knee operation. Both perfectly good reasons. We would still like to fill the two places.

You do not need any nursing skill. None. You need to be able to push a trolley up a corridor, remember who takes what, and listen to people. It turns out that forty-one years of keeping other people's ledgers straight is directly useful for remembering who takes two sugars, who has gone over to decaf, and who will not touch a ginger nut. Mr Hollis, who is a retired signalman, takes two sugars and tells me about the 1953 floods every week, slightly differently each time. I have stopped correcting the dates. I have never told him I have stopped correcting the dates.

**Getting started.** Bridget does the induction, which takes about two hours, and there is a short food hygiene course to do online, which the hospice pays for. That is all. There is no uniform and no list of things you must not say, though I have worked most of that out by myself fairly quickly.

**If you want to come and look first:** there is a volunteer open afternoon on Tuesday 24 November at two o'clock in the Willow Room. Tea and biscuits, no obligation, and nobody will ask you to commit to anything on the spot. Or ring Bridget on the volunteering line and ask her about the trolley.

Now, the honest bit, since some people assume that volunteering in a hospice must be either harrowing or frightfully skilled, and I would like to correct both.

It is not harrowing. A Thursday in the day unit is, mostly, noisy and rather jolly. It is not a sad place, although I will not pretend it is never a sad place. Bad weeks happen. People are very ill and some of them will not be here next month, and on those days the staff look after us as well as the patients, and they are very good at it. But if I painted you a picture of constant sorrow you would be signing up for the wrong thing, and you would be disappointed.

The other thing worth saying is that you will get it wrong at first. My first week I put an entire jug of milk over the trolley, the lid, the floor, one patient's cardigan. A woman called Pat laughed so hard the staff had to give her a tissue, and she said it was the best afternoon she had had in a month. I had been volunteering for about three hours. If I can survive that, you can.

Also, the bourbon biscuits always go first. We have now taken to hiding a packet for the late group, which I am aware is not in the spirit of the exercise, and which I am in no position to discuss further.

If you fancy it, come to the open afternoon on the 24th, or ring Bridget. We could do with two more, and I can promise that if you take one Thursday a fortnight and a jug of tea, you will get more out of it than I did — which is not difficult, because for eighteen months I was getting almost nothing at all.

I am not a saint. I am an old bookkeeper who likes a routine, a chat, and the fact that nobody has asked me to reconcile anything since 2021.

— *A volunteer, Thursday tea trolley*
